description: Recent Foods & Copy Meal to Another Day — a Recent tab in the Log Food sheet for one-tap re-logging of previously logged foods (most-recent-first), plus per-meal-slot copy to a different day. Derived entirely from existing FoodDiaryEntry rows; NO new table or migration. Stack: Kotlin Multiplatform + Compose Multiplatform, SQLDelight source of truth, StateHolder + StateFlow UDF. Typecheck gate: ./gradlew :composeApp:compileDebugKotlinAndroid. Tests: ./gradlew :composeApp:testDebugUnitTest (commonTest uses runSync + in-memory fakes; NO SQLDelight driver, NO coroutines-test). Full spec: tasks/prd-recent-meals.md.

userStories.title: Recent-foods query + repository method
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a query returning the most recently logged distinct foods so the Recent tab has data.
acceptanceCriteria: Add `recentFoods` query to FoodDiary.sq returning one row per distinct food, newest first (ORDER BY id DESC), with a LIMIT (?) parameter

Distinctness key = food_id when present, else lower(trim(foodName)) || '|' || lower(trim(COALESCE(brandName,''))); use subquery SELECT MAX(id) ... GROUP BY that key so a food logged N times appears once with its last-used serving/macros
No schema change / no migration — query only over the existing FoodDiaryEntry table
Add fun getRecentFoods(limit: Int): Flow<List<FoodDiaryEntry>> to FoodDiaryRepository + impl in FoodDiaryRepositoryImpl, main-safe via asFlow().mapToList(Dispatchers.Default)
Returned entries are detached templates: map toDomain then copy(id = 0, sortOrder = 0)
Update the in-memory FakeFoodDiaryRepository in commonTest (FoodDiaryReorderTest.kt) to implement getRecentFoods
Unit test in commonTest using runSync + a fake/in-memory repo: dedup keeps one row per food, ordering is most-recent-first, limit is respected
Tests pass: ./gradlew :composeApp:testDebugUnitTest
Typecheck passes: ./gradlew :composeApp:compileDebugKotlinAndroid

userStories.title: Copy-meal-slot repository operation
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a repository method that duplicates one meal slot's entries onto another date so the UI can offer Copy to day.
acceptanceCriteria: Add suspend fun copyMealToDate(sourceDate: String, mealType: String, targetDate: String) to FoodDiaryRepository + impl
Reads source slot via getEntriesByDateAndMeal; inserts a copy of each into targetDate/same mealType inside one SQLDelight transaction, reusing insertEntry

Copied entries get new ids and sortOrder appended AFTER existing target entries: start at maxSortOrderForDateMeal(targetDate, mealType) + 1; all other fields copied verbatim (id/date/sortOrder excluded)
No-op (no throw) when the source slot is empty
Update FakeFoodDiaryRepository in commonTest to implement copyMealToDate with the same append semantics
Unit test (runSync + fake): copying N entries appends N to target, source unchanged, target's pre-existing entries preserved and first
Tests pass: ./gradlew :composeApp:testDebugUnitTest
Typecheck passes: ./gradlew :composeApp:compileDebugKotlinAndroid

userStories.title: StateHolder: recents flow + copyMeal action
userStories.description: As a developer, I need StateHolder entry points for recents and copy so the UI stays unidirectional.
acceptanceCriteria: FoodDiaryStateHolder exposes recentFoods: StateFlow<List<FoodDiaryEntry>> from repository.getRecentFoods(20) via stateIn(scope, SharingStarted.WhileSubscribed(5_000), emptyList())
FoodDiaryStateHolder adds fun copyMeal(sourceDate: String, mealType: String, targetDate: String): Job that launches on its scope and calls repository.copyMealToDate
No change to existing state / weeklyTotals flows
Typecheck passes: ./gradlew :composeApp:compileDebugKotlinAndroid

userStories.title: Recent tab in Log Food sheet
userStories.description: As a user, I want a Recent tab in the food-logging sheet so I can see foods I've logged before instead of searching.
acceptanceCriteria: FoodSearchSheet/FoodSearchContent in FoodLogSheet.kt shows two segments: Search (default) and Recent
Add a recentFoods: List<FoodDiaryEntry> = emptyList() parameter to FoodSearchSheet; pass foodDiaryStateHolder.recentFoods (collected) from the addingToMeal call site in MacroDailyCounterDetail.kt
Recent tab lists rows reusing FoodResultRow styling: name, brand (if any), subtitle "{servingSizeG.roundToInt()}{servingUnit} · {calories.roundToInt()}kcal", most-recent-first
Empty state when list is empty: "No recent foods yet — log something first."
Switching tabs does not reset an in-progress search query; the Create custom food affordance stays on the Search tab only
Verify on device: build + ./gradlew :composeApp:installDebug, open Log Food, switch to Recent tab, confirm prior foods render (NOTE: dev-browser skill does not apply — this is an Android/iOS app)
Typecheck passes: ./gradlew :composeApp:compileDebugKotlinAndroid

userStories.title: One-tap add from Recent tab
userStories.description: As a user, I want tapping a recent food to add it straight to the meal slot I'm logging into, using the serving I last used.
acceptanceCriteria: Tapping a recent row invokes the sheet's onAddEntry with the template copied to the current mealType + selected date (id = 0, sortOrder = 0), carrying macros/servingSizeG/servingUnit/foodName/brandName/food_id verbatim
Goes through the existing add path (FoodDiaryStateHolder.addEntry) so a fresh id + appended sortOrder are assigned and Health Connect sync fires
Sheet dismisses on add (matches add-from-search behavior); daily totals + balance refresh via the existing onBalanceRefreshNeeded callback
Verify on device: tap a recent → entry appears in the correct slot with correct macros; daily totals update
Typecheck passes: ./gradlew :composeApp:compileDebugKotlinAndroid

userStories.title: Copy-to-day action on a meal slot
userStories.description: As a user, I want a Copy to another day action on a meal slot so I can replicate it without re-entering each food.
acceptanceCriteria: Each meal slot (Breakfast/Lunch/Dinner/Snacks) in MacroDailyCounterDetail.kt exposes a "Copy to day" action in its header, enabled only when the slot has >= 1 entry
Tapping it opens the existing DatePickerDialog to choose the target date
On confirm, calls foodDiaryStateHolder.copyMeal(currentDate, mealType, targetDate) then onBalanceRefreshNeeded(); shows snackbar "Copied {Slot} to {targetDate}" via the existing snackbar host
Copying to the same day appends a duplicate set (allowed; no special guard)
Verify on device: copy Lunch to tomorrow → tomorrow's Lunch shows the same entries appended; today's Lunch unchanged
Typecheck passes: ./gradlew :composeApp:compileDebugKotlinAndroid
